dedupe_keys.name: coal power plant reinvestment visualization tool

description: The Coal Power Plant Reinvestment Visualization Tool is a public database and map of US coal power plants that have closed or are set to retire, with nearby infrastructure relevant to redevelopment. It was produced by the National Energy Technology Laboratory and Pacific Northwest National Laboratory for state and local economic development officials, project developers and plant owners looking for reinvestment in solar, wind, manufacturing or nuclear. It covers plants where at least one generator uses or used coal, including planned retirements through 2058 based on EIA data from 2024, together with electric transmission lines, EPA brownfield sites assessed with federal funding, petroleum terminals, ports, railroads and other layers, with predefined and user-set queries. Coverage is the United States at plant level. The tool is accessible online on the Energy Communities website and listed on NETL's Energy Data eXchange (updated April 2025) under a Creative Commons Attribution licence at no cost. Caveats: the tool will be updated periodically, and the energycommunities.gov page could not be opened from this environment on the day, so details come from the EDX record. Simulation uses are siting replacement generation and grid reuse for capacity planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
